title: Niryasa 1. The Description of the Branches of Sri Acharya Prabhu
html:
Opening verses and salutations; Mahaprabhu manifests two shaktis — Sri Rupa (the books) and Srinivasa (their spreading); Srinivasa as the wish-fulfilling tree and his branches; life in Yajigrama, the Gosvamis' books and his daily round; the order to describe Srinivasa's branches; the conversion of Ramachandra Kaviraja; branches and sub-branches: family, disciples in Kanchanagaria; the theft of the books, Vyasa Acharya and Vira Hambira with his songs; disciples in Vishnupura and everywhere

1Glory to Sri Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-chandra! May Hari, the son of Shachi, radiant with a lustre lovelier than gold, ever be manifest in the cave of your heart — He who out of mercy descended in the age of Kali to bestow what had not been bestowed for a long time: the exalted, radiant rasa of service, the wealth of devotion to Himself.1

2Sri Krishna — Krishna Chaitanya, with Sanatana and Rupa, with Gopala and the Raghunathas, the beloved of Vraja — protect me!

3I bow to Gopala Bhatta, whose heart is flooded with eternal prema (the prema of Sanatana), who is marked by friendship with Sri Rupa, whose only life is Radha-ramana, and who grants the desire of those who worship.

4I worship Srinivasa Prabhu, dear to Radha-ramana, who established the scriptures of rasa and leads to the goal of parakiya.2

5Glory, glory to Mahaprabhu, glory to the ocean of mercy!
Glory, glory to Nityananda, glory to the friend of the fallen!

6Glory, glory to Advaita-chandra, the ocean of compassion!
Glory, glory to the Lord's associates headed by Srivasa!

7Glory to Sri Rupa and Sanatana, embodiments of prema!
Glory to Sri Gopala Bhatta, the well of prema-bhakti!

8Glory to Srila Raghunatha Bhatta — be merciful to me!
Glory to Raghunatha Dasa on the bank of Radha-kunda!

9Glory, glory to Jiva Gosani, the treasury of compassion!
Glory to Sri Acharya Prabhu, the limit of all virtues!

10Glory, glory to Ramachandra Kaviraja and Govinda:
the world rejoices in the rasa of their lives!

11Glory to the Vaishnava Gosanis, purifiers of the fallen!
Be merciful, my masters: I take shelter of you.

12Listen, listen, devotees, with one mind:
Mahaprabhu manifested two shaktis,

13to fulfil the cherished desire of His heart
and for the joy of revealing it on earth.

14Empowering Sri Rupa, He manifested the books,
and His heart rejoiced as that shakti was revealed.

15Thus He manifested the greatest of great treasures —
the one through whom hundreds of thousands of verses appeared.3

16And so that this rare treasure might be made known,
He came and manifested shakti in Srinivasa.

17Having manifested the two shaktis, He rejoiced at heart;
tasting this, the living beings became free.

18To make that rare treasure known,
He came and spread it through the shakti in Srinivasa.

19Such is my Acharya Thakura Srinivasa:
in the shelter of this wish-fulfilling tree the living beings' sufferings were removed.

20Srinivasa descended in the form of a wish-fulfilling tree
and out of mercy delivered the living beings.

21Ramachandra Kaviraja is a branch of that tree:
how could I write of his endless virtues?

22Charming is the form of Ramachandra Kaviraja;
his virtues are to the world what the tree is.

23His younger brother is most virtuous —
his name is Sri Govinda Kaviraja.

24Another branch of the tree is named Govinda Chakravarti;
these three branches are the abode of every virtue.

25Beginning with them, the branches of the tree
are endless and boundless — who could write of them?

26Now I shall name the sub-branches of the tree:
Sri Balarama Kaviraja and the other sub-branches.

27Its branches and sub-branches spread over the world;
from the sidelong glance of compassion the leaves unfolded.

28Various blessed bhavas blossomed as flowers,
and the pure bhava of parakiya filled it with fragrance.

29Thus the tree became most fragrant,
and on it ripened the fruit of pure prema-bhakti.

30Listen, listen, devotees — this is my request:
water the tree with the water of hearing and the other forms of service.

31Casting far away karma, jnana and the rest,
all of you taste the fruit, filling yourselves to the throat.

32Srinivasa was adorned as the wish-fulfilling tree:
in Gauda he made manifest hundreds of thousands of verses.3

33All the books Sri Rupa Gosvami composed,
all the books Sanatana Gosvami revealed,

34what Sri Bhatta Gosani (Gopala Bhatta) revealed,
and Raghunatha Bhatta and Raghunatha Dasa,

35the collection of books written by Sri Jiva Gosvami,
and all the rasa-filled books the Kaviraja made4 —

36taking all these books to Gauda, Prabhu
spread them freely, with joy in his heart.

37Srinivasa, like the wind, brought the clouds of books —
he who carried them with great effort.

38Bringing the clouds of books from among the hills of Vraja,
he watered the field of Gauda with the water of prema.

39The living beings — crops scorched by the sun of Kali —
received life from the rain of Krishna-prema.

40The rain-clouds of prema filled the earth,
and the devotee-peacocks dance, intoxicated, intoxicated.

41When Prabhu took up residence in Yajigrama,
Vaishnavas came and gathered round him every day.

42To them all he speaks of prema in bhakti-yoga;
he cured them all of the disease of jnana and karma.

43So many days pass in the bliss of prema;
floating in the rasa of Krishna-prema, he sings, full of bhava.

44At the request of the Vaishnavas he married,
and some days later he married again.5

45He studies the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu and the Ujjvala,
the Vidagdha-madhava, the Lalita-madhava and the rest;

46the Hari-bhakti-vilasa and the Bhagavatamrita,
the commentary on the Tenth Canto and the Dashama-charita;

47the Mathura-mahatmya and many collections of hymns,
the Hamsa-duta, the Uddhava-sandesha and the rest — all of them;

48the Six Sandarbhas, the Toshani on the Tenth Canto of the Bhagavata;
the Gitavali and the Virudavali he reads in order;

49the Mukta-charitra and the Krishna-karnamrita,
the Brahma-samhita and others, and the Gopi-premamrita.

50How many names do I know — and the books run to hundreds of thousands of verses!
Unceasingly he studies the Madhava-mahotsava and others.6

51He read and expounded the books to the assembly of Vaishnavas,
immersed in the nectar of prema night and day.

52Counting, he chants Hari-nama for one prahara;
another prahara passes in the study of the books.

53Two yamas7 are kirtana of Radha, Krishna and Govinda;
unceasingly he floats in the prema of remembering the pastimes.

54Chandidasa, Vidyapati, the Sri Gita-govinda,
Raya's drama8 — these books he sings in supreme bliss.

55At night, with the devotees, the rasa and other pastimes;
he taught songs — the jubilation of bhakti and prema.

56By day, service of the shalagrama and service of Tulasi:
with supreme devotion he waters her.

57Meditation on Radha and Krishna, the mantra and the names of Them both —
thus he always remembers the pastimes and keeps them in mind.

58Saying "Sri Rupa, Sanatana", he lets out a great cry;
saying "Sri Gopala Bhatta", he sobs aloud.

59Saying "Radha-kunda, Krishna-kunda", he faints again and again;
saying "Mount Govardhana", he cries, "Alas, alas!"

60Thus day and night pass in the bliss of prema,
and tasting the nectar of prema, he rejoices at heart.

61The pious think it good, the impious laugh;
yet now all those people float in bliss.

62He sings the glories of Gaura and of Prabhu Nityananda;
thus day and night compassion arises.

63Now I shall tell of the branches of Sri Acharya Prabhu,
by merely remembering whose names prema is awakened.

64The proof of this is a verse: I worship the great host of branches of Srila Srinivasa Prabhu: by merely remembering their names, Krishna-prema arises.

65All the branches of Sri Acharya Prabhu
two persons have described in verse:

66what Thakura Mahashaya described,
and what Karnapura Kaviraja composed.9

67Following the verses of these two great souls,
my Prabhu ordered me to render them in payar.10

68I took Prabhu's order on my head, but many days passed;
and then, through the Vaishnavas, he ordered it again.

69The order is stronger than I — so I describe this;
whether it is good or bad I cannot tell.

70I am worthless and dull-witted: what do I know of description?
Forgive my fault, Prabhu — I take shelter.

71The words of Prabhu's order and the Vaishnavas' command —
this I have understood especially in my heart.

72What more can I say — I am the foremost of fools;
the Vaishnava Gosanis will forgive me everything.

73Placing on my head the dust of the feet of you all,
I shall tell a little of this in payar.

74Do not count it a fault if something is told out of order;
I bow to the feet of all and rejoice.

75Now I shall tell of Prabhu's branches and sub-branches;
forgiving my offences, please listen.

76One day, on the western side of his house,
he sat on the bank of the pond.

77Just then someone came along riding in a palanquin:
he was on the road, newly married, and musicians were playing.

78Seeing a form like Manmatha's, Prabhu thinks:
"Such wondrous beauty I have never seen!

79His complexion is like a golden ketaki flower,
his broad chest most lovely;

80his belly is handsome, with a line of fine hair;
his feet and hands are red;

81his face is beautiful as the full moon,
his nose high and his teeth beautiful;

82his lips are charming, surpassing the bimba fruit,
his lotus eyes shine enchantingly;

83his neck like a conch, his waist slender, his hair curling,
his thighs like inverted plantain trunks, his knees well formed."

84He wore silk, a garland of flowers on his neck,
sandal paste on his body. Seeing him, Prabhu asked:

85"Who is he — Kamadeva or one of the Ashvini-kumaras?
Or some god, or the son of a gandharva?"

86So, gazing at his form again and again,
Prabhu began to speak, and his mercy doubled:

87"If, having received such a body, he worships Krishna,
then this body will bear fruit and not perish in vain.

88Tell me, you who are with him, brothers:
in which village is his home, where does he live?

89What is his caste and what is his name? Tell me in detail."
Bowing, they told him everything:

90"This is Ramachandra Kaviraja, a great pandita:
who can equal him? He is like Vachaspati, famed like Sarasvati.

91He was born in a worthy Vaidya family, foremost in fame,
a great physician; he is called 'Conqueror of the Quarters'.11

92His home is in Kumaranagara; his name is renowned."
Hearing this, Prabhu joyfully returned to his house.

93All that Prabhu had said the Kaviraja heard attentively,
and having heard, went joyfully to his own home.

94Being most composed, he gave no answer,
but began to meditate in his heart on Prabhu's feet.

95Thus he passed the day at home with difficulty,
and at night came to Prabhu's door.

96He passed the night with difficulty in a brahmana's house,
and in the morning came and fell at Prabhu's feet.

97Weeping and weeping, he rolls on the ground,
lying on the earth like a tree torn up by the roots.

98In a choked voice he says: "Give me the shade of your feet!
Do not spurn my scorched soul!"12

99Prabhu rose, lifted him by his creeper-like arms,
and joyfully, out of mercy, embraced him tightly.

100"May you have Krishna-bhakti," he blessed him,
and, faltering with prema, began to speak:

101"Birth after birth you are my friend and helper;
merciful Providence has brought you to me."

102Saying this, he gave him the mantra of Radha-Krishna
and told him again and again the pastimes of Radha-Krishna.

103In a few days he read the books with him,
and at last, blessing him, gave him this instruction:

104"You are in every way my own self;
may you become full of prema by the mercy of Govinda.

105In Vrindavana there was one like you:
Providence gave me that treasure — his name is Narottama.

106For a long time we lived together;
by giving me you, the Merciful One has given me two eyes."

107Thus out of mercy he instructed him
and brought him together with Narottama Thakura.

108Between Narottama and Ramachandra prema grew —
such prema that they became one soul in two bodies.

109Then Prabhu showed mercy to Sri Govinda Kaviraja:
he became a disciple, and Prabhu empowered him.

110He is (Ramachandra's) younger brother, a great pandita;
both are maha-bhagavatas, their hearts full of prema.

111To compose songs of the pastimes of Radha-Krishna in the manner of rasa verses
(Prabhu) ordered the Kaviraja with great mercy.13

112He composed his own verses and songs in many styles,
and the earth floated in the nectar of prema of those songs.

113To the wives of the two Kavirajas
he showed mercy with a merciful heart.

114Then Prabhu showed mercy to Divyasimha:14
receiving Prabhu's mercy, he became most blessed.

115Then to Prabhu's two virtuous wives
Prabhu, the jewel of virtues, showed mercy.

116The elder is named Srimati Ishvari Thakurani:
what can I say of her incomparable virtues?

117The younger is Srimati Gauranga-priya Thakurani:
how could I describe her life?

118Both are most loving and virtuous,
both are expert (vidagdha), both a treasury of rasa.

119I cannot describe the summit of their bhajana;
both are most composed and sweet in character.

120Most dear to Prabhu, most virtuous,
both are the limit of expertise, sweet in form.

121The bhajana of both is pure raganuga, exclusive;
the bhajana of both is wholly in the bhava of parakiya.15

122What can I say of the steadfast bhajana of both:
of karma, jnana and the like they will not even hear.

123I, lowly and worthless — how could I explain it?
Both beloveds of Prabhu are equal to Prabhu himself.

124Their disciples and disciples' disciples flooded the world;
further on I shall carefully tell of this.

125The eldest son is named Sri Vrindavana Acharya:
Prabhu, the abode of virtues, showed him mercy.

126Prabhu's middle son is Radhakrishna Acharya:
what can I say of his virtues — everything in him is wondrous.

127Prabhu, the treasury of virtues, showed him mercy:
he is the wondrous limit of virtues.

128The youngest son is named Sri Gati-Govinda:
Prabhu showed him mercy with a merciful heart.

129Sri Gati-Govinda Prabhu wrote down the line
of his gurus in a verse of his own, eagerly and gladly.

130This is the verse: The bee at the lotus feet of Sri Chaitanya is Gopala Bhatta Prabhu; the glorious bee at his lotus feet is the one named Sri Srinivasa, known to all people in all lands as Acharya Prabhu; and the one whose glory is the shelter of his lotus feet is called Gati-Govinda.

131He who took shelter at the lotus feet of Sri Krishna Chaitanya
and, becoming a bee, ever delights there —

132Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosani, filled with mercy,
showed boundless mercy to Sri Acharya Prabhu.

133The shelter of the lotus feet of Sri Acharya Prabhu —
of this Sri Gati-Govinda speaks in his verse.

134He is a great giver, great and virtuous;
his disciples and disciples' disciples flooded the world.

135All this I shall tell in detail later;
now I shall briefly tell of Prabhu's branches.

136Then Prabhu's own daughter named Hemalata:
to her he graciously showed mercy.

137She had many disciples and disciples' disciples;
she flooded the whole earth with the nectar of prema.

138Another daughter is Krishnapriya Thakurani:
he, the jewel of mercy, gave her the shelter of his feet.

139Another daughter, whose name is Kanchana-latika:
to her too the merciful one gave the shelter of his feet.

140Then Prabhu showed mercy to Kanchanagaria:
coming there, he showed mercy to Sri Dasa Thakura.16

141He is a maha-bhagavata, a great pandita,
who always remained near Prabhu.

142Jayakrishna, Jagadisha and Shyama-vallabha Acharya —
his three sons, great and noble in virtue.

143These three worthies are vessels of the mercy of Sri Ishvara;17
they are maha-bhagavatas, abodes of prema.

144There too is his eldest, Sri Gokula Dasa:
the Thakura showed him mercy with great joy.

145Carrying water on his head, he serves Krishna;
no one can understand his prema and its expressions.

146To his son, Sri Krishnavallabha Thakura —
seeing how beautiful he was, Prabhu showed mercy.

147He received mercy as a child;
he is a maha-bhagavata and made many disciples.

148There too, to Sri Narasimha Kaviraja
Prabhu showed mercy: he gave him mantra, investing him with shakti.

149He is a great pandita and meditates on Prabhu;
his prema, its expressions and his virtues cannot be understood.

150He had many disciples and disciples' disciples.
Then Prabhu showed mercy to Raghunatha.

151Ramakrishna Chattaraja is one of Prabhu's branches:
how can I write of his greatness and virtues?

152Devoted to Hari-nama, he always takes Hari-nama:
counting, he chants the name always, without rest.

153His son is Gopijanavallabha Chattaraja,
who is renowned in the world.

154His love for Prabhu is great, and Prabhu is merciful to him;
I cannot describe his greatness.

155To him, mercifully and graciously,
Prabhu gave in marriage his daughter Srila Hemalata.18

156Sri Kumuda Chattaraja is a dear servant of Prabhu:
apart from Prabhu's feet he has no other concern.

157His son is Sri Chaitanya Chattaraja,
a vessel of Prabhu's mercy, king of great devotees.

158To him Prabhu, filled with mercy, showed mercy
and gave him in marriage his daughter Srila Krishnapriya.

159Rajendra Bandyopadhyaya, the Chattaraja's son-in-law —
to him too Prabhu graciously showed mercy.

160I cannot write of his countless virtues:
he is always absorbed in the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.

161His love for Prabhu is great, Prabhu is his life;
he constantly, without pause, chants Hari-nama.

162The Chattaraja's two daughters are both virtuous,
of gentle form, both most pure and serene.

163Then Prabhu showed mercy to Sri Malati:
receiving Prabhu's mercy, she became most blessed.

164To the other daughter, named Sri Phuljhi Thakurani,
Prabhu, the jewel of virtues, showed mercy.

165Then the one called Kalanidhi Chattaraja:
he always chants Hari-nama — that is his occupation.

166Prabhu says: "You are most dear to Chaitanya;
chant a hundred thousand names, making it your rule."

167Most dear to Prabhu, foremost among servants,
is Vrindavana Chattaraja, the beloved servant, his very life.

168What can I say of the bhajana of them all?
As I speak, waves of an ocean of happiness rise in my heart.

169There too he showed most pure mercy to a varna-brahmana:19
filled with mercy, he showed him mercy.

170His name is Sri Gopala Dasa; showing him mercy,
Prabhu ordered him to deliver his own community.

171In the village of Kanchanagaria Prabhu's devotees
each keep the rule of a hundred thousand names of Hari.

172By day they do not chant the name, but at night, sitting down,
tying their hair with a cord to the rafter, they sit and chant the name.20

173They are all Prabhu's life, and Prabhu is the life of them all;
that place is most dear to him, and he never leaves it.

174A disciple of Gopala Dasa Thakura, a worthy man,
is Sri Gopimohana Dasa of Mirzapur.

175He is a maha-bhagavata — what is there to say of him?
His disciple is Shyamadasa, who lives in Khadgrama.

176Prabhu showed mercy to one named Govinda Chakravarti,
whose bhajana from childhood was incomparable.

177His body is the embodiment of prema, his name renowned:
known as "Bhavaka Chakravarti", of the village of Borakuli.

178His disciples and disciples' disciples filled the world;
later I shall tell of the fame that came of it.

179His wife is virtuous and wise,
a vessel of the mercy of Sri Ishvari, of excellent conduct.

180She takes a hundred thousand names of Hari
and constantly tells of the deeds of Mahaprabhu.

181Sri Gopala Bhatta, Sri Rupa and Sanatana,
and the feet of Acharya Prabhu are her constant meditation.

182How much more can I expound the virtues of this Thakurani,
whose way of bhajana is renowned in the world?

183(Govinda Chakravarti's) eldest son is named Rajavallabha Chakravarti:
what can I say of his incomparable virtues?

184I cannot describe his life:
apart from Prabhu's feet there is nothing else in his heart.

185The two other sons became disciples of their mother —
Radhavinoda and Kishori Dasa, devoted to bhakti.

186To Karnapura Kaviraja Prabhu showed mercy —
he who was blessed in describing Prabhu's branches.21

187I cannot describe his boundless bhajana:
he is always absorbed in service performed in the mind.

188He takes a hundred thousand names of Hari
and so lives, his mind immersed in happiness.

189Then Prabhu showed mercy to Vana-Vishnupura:
many disciples of his appeared there.

190Then Sri Acharya showed mercy to Vyasa
and, making him his servant, taught him much.

191Those confidential virtues cannot be told:
he is most learned and full of prema.

192He had many branches and sub-branches;
those maha-bhagavatas delivered the world.

193Sri Vamshidasa Thakura, a worthy man,
is a dear branch of Prabhu, sweet in disposition.

194Devoted to Hari-nama, he always takes Hari-nama:
counting, he chants the name always, without rest.

195Sri Gopaladasa Thakura is one of Prabhu's branches,
most dear to Prabhu; his virtues cannot be written down.

196His home is in Budhuipara; he is a kirtana singer of Sri Krishna,
by whose kirtana even stone melts.

197Sri Rupa Ghataka is a dear servant of Prabhu:
apart from the names of Radha and Krishna he has no other concern.

198Then Prabhu showed mercy to Raghunandana Dasa
and gladly gave him the title "Ghataka".22

199Both Ghatakas are most virtuous:
both know Prabhu's feet as their all.

200Sudhakara Mandala is one of Prabhu's servants;
his wife Shyamapriya is a vessel of mercy.

201Their son is the virtuous Radhavallabha Mandala:
apart from Hari-nama he has no other concern.

202Then Prabhu showed mercy to Kamadeva Mandala:
receiving Prabhu's mercy, he became most blessed.

203Who can tell of his hidden bhava?
The pastimes of Radha and Krishna appear in his heart.

204He always takes Hari-nama,
and Prabhu's two feet shine in his heart.

205Then Prabhu showed mercy to Gopala Mandala,
whose faith in Prabhu's feet is most pure.

206Prabhu's two fathers-in-law are most wise;
the lives of the two cannot be described.

207Both are most pure in conduct and spotless in body;
they have nothing but meditation on Mahaprabhu's feet.

208Sri Gopala Chakravarti is a dear servant of Prabhu:
tears flow from his eyes without rest; in kirtana he dances.

209The other father-in-law is Sri Raghunandana Chakravarti:
receiving Prabhu's mercy, he became renowned.23

210Of Prabhu's two brothers-in-law — listen:
both became vessels of Prabhu's mercy.

211The elder is the worthy Shyamadasa Chakravarti,
a vessel of Prabhu's mercy, with a merciful heart.

212He is a scholar of the Srimad-Bhagavatam
and is wildly intoxicated with prema at the verses of the Bhagavata.

213His younger brother is most devoted, a worthy man;
I shall tell where his home is: he lives in Faridpur.

214Ramacharana Chakravarti is Prabhu's servant;
how many of his disciples shall I name?

215He chants a hundred thousand names of Hari, counting them,
and speaks of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna, relishing them.

216He is passionately fond of kirtana and always dances in it;
tears always flow from his eyes, for he is full of prema.

217He is the life of the Vaishnavas, like a vessel of tenderness;
who can count his countless virtues?

218A vessel of Prabhu's mercy is one Chatta Krishnadasa:
he chants a hundred thousand names of Hari; all his faith is in the name.

219There is no end to his servants:
all are devoted to Hari-nama, all are virtuous.

220One named Vanamali Dasa, born in a Vaidya family,24
a dear servant of Prabhu — who can know his heart?

221Sri Mohana Dasa, born in a Vaidya family,
whose steadfast bhajana is most pure —

222great and worthy, sweet in disposition,
most dear to Prabhu, with a merciful heart.

223Sri Radhavallabha Dasa is Prabhu's servant,
a maha-bhagavata, rich in bhajana.

224Most dear to Prabhu is Sri Mathura Dasa:
he always chants Hari-nama with great joy.

225Radhakrishna Dasa is a dear servant of Prabhu:
unceasingly his tears of prema flow; in kirtana he dances.

226Sri Ramana Dasa is a vessel of Prabhu's mercy,
on whose lips the nectar of Hari-nama always remains.

227Another servant of Prabhu is named Ramadasa:
ever in the madness of prema he dances and takes the name of Hari.

228Sri Kavivallabha is Prabhu's own servant:
in prema he sings the names of Radha and Krishna with great joy.

229Many books he copied out for Prabhu:
his writing is like strings of pearls; he is a great calligrapher.

230Vanamali Dasa's father, Sri Gopala Dasa,
is Prabhu's servant, most pure in speech.

231Then Prabhu showed mercy to Shyamadasa Chatta:
he is a maha-bhagavata and received Prabhu's mercy.

232There too is Sri Atmarama, a dear servant of Prabhu:
he always chants Hari-nama, indifferent to the world.

233To Sri Nakadi Dasa he showed great mercy:
he made Prabhu's feet his all.

234Sri Gopiramana Dasa is a worthy Vaidya:
boundless mercy of Prabhu came to him.

235He loves Hari-nama and takes the name of Hari;
he sings of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna — an abode of great prema.

236His home is in Goyasa; he is a fine connoisseur of rasa:
he always speaks of Krishna's rasa, in which prema abounds.

237Sri Durgadasa is Prabhu's own servant:
he always chants Hari-nama with joy in his heart.

238Then Prabhu showed mercy to Shyamadasa Kaviraja,
whose bhajana is manifest in the world.

239Then Prabhu showed mercy to Raghunatha Dasa,
who, receiving Prabhu's mercy, rejoiced in his heart.

240To Kumudananda Thakura Prabhu showed mercy,
who, receiving Prabhu's mercy, attained the goal of life.

241Sri Ramadasa Thakura is a dear servant of Prabhu:
apart from meditation on Radha and Krishna he has no other concern.

242Radhavallabha Dasa Thakura is simple and generous,
in whose heart is meditation on Prabhu's feet.

243Gokulananda Dasa Chakravarti is a worthy man:
Prabhu, with a merciful heart, showed him mercy.

244Another servant is Sri Gokulananda Dasa:
he always chants Hari-nama; all his faith is in the name.

245Then he showed mercy to Sri Gopaladasa Thakura:
receiving Prabhu's mercy, he became most blessed.

246Then Prabhu showed mercy to Shyamadasa:
he is the glory of the Chatta family, of supreme devotion.

247Then Prabhu set out for the darshana of Purushottama25
and went joyfully along forest roads.

248One day he stayed the night in a village;
robbers, taking (his books) for jewels, seized them.

249The thieves carried off the books on their way;
then Prabhu went to the king for the sake of the books.

250At that time a brahmana, Vyasa Chakravarti,
was reciting the Puranas to the king with great feeling.

251For reciting the Puranas the king gave him the name "Acharya":
from then on he became known in the world as Acharya.

252Just then the brahmana is reading the Bhramara-gita;
hearing the explanation, Prabhu laughs, standing some way off.

253Then Prabhu entered the assembly and sat down,
and, seated, refuted the whole explanation.

254Then the king's heart rejoiced greatly:
his mind became absorbed in the wish to hear the explanation.

255The king humbly requests:
"Please explain it yourself, be merciful!"

256Prabhu explained the verse according to the Gosvamis;
hearing it, the king became as if mad.

257Then he bowed and fell at his feet:
"Prabhu, be merciful to me, I take shelter!

258Alas, alas! Such an explanation I have never heard!"
Crying aloud, he weeps, fallen on the ground.

259In a choked voice he says: "Hear me, sir:
be merciful, take pity on me!"

260Prabhu asks: "What is this brahmana's name?"
The king replies: "Sri Vyasa Acharya.

261His name from the beginning was 'Acharya'."
Prabhu said: "The name 'Acharya' suits him well."

262Then Prabhu speaks to the king:
"May Vrajendra-nandana be merciful to you."

263The Malla king named Sri Vira Hambira —
to him Prabhu, merciful and profound, showed mercy.

264He gained steadfast bhakti for Krishna's feet;
he entrusted all the affairs of the kingdom to Prabhu.

265What can I say of the shelter of that Prabhu's feet!
The shelter of those feet destroys both desires and the craving for liberation;

266whoever sees those feet, touches them, takes shelter of them and serves them
easily obtains the treasure of the nectar of prema.

267In that land of Vana-Vishnupura very many
became his disciples — they cannot be counted.

268I have not written this out in detail in the book —
only the little I heard from the lips of Srimati.26

269Born in the Karana family,27 most pure in conduct,
two brothers, sons of Karunakara Dasa,

270always wrote the documents in Prabhu's house;
therefore the merciful one gave them the name "Bishvas".28

271To the elder, the worthy Sri Janakirama Dasa,
merciful Prabhu showed mercy.

272To his younger brother Prasada Dasa he showed mercy:
receiving Prabhu's mercy, both became great devotees.

273Formerly their surname was Majumdar;
now the surname "Bishvas", given by Prabhu, became established.

274There too he showed mercy to Vallavi Kavipati:
receiving the shelter of his feet, he became pious.

275He always chants Hari-nama, keeping a rule:
until he has chanted a hundred thousand names of Hari he does not eat.

276He lives near Prabhu; Prabhu is his life;
he entrusted his house and household to Prabhu.

277His two elder brothers are worthy men:
to the eldest, Ramadasa, Prabhu was merciful,

278and to the middle one, Gopaladasa, he showed mercy:
thus Prabhu's great mercy came upon the three brothers.

279To Sri Vallabha Thakura, who lived in the village of Deuli,
he showed abundant mercy.

280In his house Prabhu stayed at first,
and therefore Prabhu's love for him was especially great.

281When from his lips Prabhu heard the news of the books' whereabouts
and recovered the stolen books, Prabhu's soul was comforted.

282Together with him he went to the king;
by his direction he obtained the great treasure, the books.29

283Therefore Prabhu showed him mercy
and, placing his foot on his head, said:

284"May Sri Radha-ramana be merciful to you,
and Sri Govinda-jiu and Madana-mohana,

285Sri Gopinatha, Rupa and Sanatana,
Sri Gopala Bhatta and the feet of Sri Jiva,

286Raghunatha Bhatta and Raghunatha Dasa —
may they be merciful to you with great joy!

287Sri Krishnadasa and Lokanatha Gosani —
may they all cast their merciful glance upon you!

288May they all fulfil your desires:
without effort you will obtain the great treasure of prema."

289Filled with mercy towards him, Prabhu stayed on
and joyfully took up residence in his house.

290Taking with him Vallavi Kaviraja and others,
he went with a glad heart to the king's palace.

291Seeing Prabhu, the king rose joyfully
and fell prostrate on the ground, touching it with the eight limbs.

292Prabhu placed his foot on the king's head
and, pleased, sat down on the seat.

293Introducing all his companions,
he greeted each fittingly, well pleased.

294For some time they talked of Krishna;
hearing it, the king's mind rejoiced.

295An ocean of bliss surged in the king's heart;
with cries of joy he clasped Prabhu's feet:

296"My birth has become fruitful — I have obtained your sight!"
The sight of those feet fulfils all desires.

297Thus, having stayed some time in the assembly,
Prabhu, pleased, returned to his lodging.

298The king went to his own quarters and rested;
lying down, the king began to reflect.

299He thinks, "I shall establish the service of Krishna,"
and in a dream he clearly sees (the Lord) in the form of Kalachand.30

300There too the form of his own Prabhu appears to the king;
seeing the beauty of both Prabhus, he reflects in his heart.

301As soon as he sees it, he begins to describe the beauty of both —
so that nectar flows in every syllable.

302On the two Prabhus he composed two padas,
by the tasting of which the bliss of prema thickens.

303In his dream the king recites the padas, and the queen, hearing them,
passed the whole night in tears.

304Hearing those wondrous padas,
the heart of the chief queen became absorbed in bhava.

305Then the king woke and sat up on his bed,
meditating in his heart on the lotus feet of his Prabhu.

306Saying "Rupa, Sanatana!" he cries out again and again;
saying "Sri Bhatta Gosani!" he laments.

307Awake, the maharaja cannot calm his mind:
the form he had seen shines in his heart.

308Now he laments, now he thinks to himself:
"The dream is broken — where has such a vision gone?"

309Awake, the maharaja sees that form:
he gazes in bliss on the beauty of his own Prabhu's form.

310He sees Prabhu saying: "Serve this One;
be steady, and you will see a wondrous form."

311The maharaja rejoices, immersed in happiness.
Just then the chief queen fell at his feet:

312"What wondrous padas you have composed, O king!
Make me blessed — let me hear them!"

313The king says: "I have composed no padas."
The queen says: "O king, do not deceive me!

314Do not deceive me, O king, gladden my mind,
or else life will not remain in my body."

315Then the king understood: without Prabhu's mercy
how could such a wondrous bhava have arisen in her?

316Then the king, pleased, said:
"Hear this pada with joy."

317This is the pada: My Prabhu Srinivasa has fulfilled my hope: apart from you I have no other refuge. I was a worm of sense objects, everything tasted sweet to me; you rid me of my royal pride. (1) I was drinking poison — you turned everything around and showed me a stream of nectar. My mind cries, "Beloved, beloved!" — everything around disquiets me; such is your dealing. (2) Radha's feet are the treasure-store of happiness: you made me a maidservant at those feet, you bound my heart to Gora's feet. Together with Sri Radha-ramana you showed me the bower-house, you revealed to me the love of the Two. (3) I go to the bank of the Yamuna: on the shore the sakhis run about, Radha and Kanu sport happily. The heart of this Vira Hambira ever meditates on Vraja, where bees fly by hundreds of thousands. (4)31

318(The second pada:) Listen, friend of my heart! The Dark One with lotus eyes — what he has done to me I myself do not know. My heart feels so strange, everything disquiets me: by loving I have lost my life. (1) Having heard of him I saw the Dark One — and seeing him I found a burning; there is no water to quench it. I brought aguru and sandal, ground them and smeared my body — the fire in my heart does not go out. (2) When I sit, he comes and makes me rise, leads me to the bank of the Yamuna. What to do, what not to do — I am always pining to death, not for a moment can I be still. (3) My mother-in-law and sister-in-law always take me for a thief; the master of the house does not even look at me. The heart of this Vira Hambira, follower of Srinivasa, has drowned at the feet of Kalachand. (4)32

319Listening and listening, the queen's joy increased;
her body grew limp in the transport of bhava, and prema rose.

320Her heart trembles continually and cannot be restrained;
"What have I heard!" the queen cries, "alas, alas!"

321When the queen's mind had grown calm,
she made many entreaties to the king:

322"Maharaja! Accept me under your care:
give me shelter at Srinivasa's feet."

323The king understood in his heart: without Prabhu's mercy
how could such a wondrous bhava have arisen?

324"The queen is fortunate," the king thinks to himself;
"it seems fate has at last become most gracious to me."

325"There is no limit to this good fortune," he says again and again;
in his heart the king understood that this was Prabhu's doing.

326Then the king, pleased, sent for Prabhu
and, joyful, fell and rolled on the ground.

327He told Prabhu's feet everything that had happened;
hearing it, Prabhu understood it fully in his heart.

328Then, when Prabhu came to the chief queen,
the queen fell at his feet and began to speak:

329"Prabhu, accept me now;
forgive my offences, Prabhu, and accept me.

330You have descended to deliver the fallen;
I know, Prabhu, you will deliver even such a sinner as I."

331Seeing the queen's entreaty, Prabhu was greatly pleased
and, filled with joy, gave her the shade of his feet.

332First he lets her hear the mantra of Hari-nama,
then he has her accept the mantra of the Divine Couple.

333Giving her worship with the kama-gayatri and the kama-bija,
he explains in detail about the group of manjaris:

334"This is the parakiya-lila; without the group of manjaris
the rasa of parakiya can never be attained.

335Without following them all, Vraja is not reached —
this I tell you with certainty.

336This bhava is pure and most spotless,
like Jambu-nadi gold, supremely radiant.

337I have told you in detail what is in my heart:
worship Krishna's feet, casting karma and the like far away.

338In the siddha-deha perform service in the mind,
and in the external body always hear and chant.33

339With a pure heart always serve the feet of the Vaishnavas,
and without effort you will attain the feet of Radha-Govinda."

340Having given all this instruction in worship,
Prabhu was pleased in mind and joyful at heart.

341Then Prabhu showed mercy to the king's son:
rejoicing, Prabhu gave him the shade of his feet.

342The heir apparent is named Sri Dhadi Hambira;
he is a vessel of Prabhu's mercy, a king among great devotees.

343Then the king established the service of Kalachand
and, seeing the beauty of His holy form, was immersed in bliss.

344He joyfully gazes on the beauty of Kalachand's form;
Prabhu himself joyfully performed the abhisheka.

345The king unceasingly serves the Vaishnavas.
This is all I have told of the king's life.

346Hearing of the king's spiritual path, Sri Jiva Gosani
there and then gave him the name Sri Gopaladasa.34

347Of the mercy to Vyasacharya I have written above:
Prabhu made him his own purohita.

348Then the wife of Sri Vyasa Acharya:
Prabhu, the jewel of virtues, showed her mercy.

349Her name is Indumukhi Thakurani:
how can I tell of her spiritual life?

350Her son is the worthy Shyamadasa Chakravarti:
merciful Prabhu showed him mercy.

351Prabhu shows mercy to Bhagavan Kavivara:
he is a pandita, a connoisseur of rasa, most composed.

352Then Prabhu showed mercy to Narayana Kavi:
when he took shelter, Prabhu gave him the shade of his feet.

353He is the brother of Sri Nrisimha Kaviraja:
the ocean of his greatness is beyond words.

354Vasudeva Kaviraja is most virtuous:
his heart is wholly and steadfastly devoted to Krishna's feet.

355Filled with mercy, Prabhu showed him mercy
and, giving him the shade of his feet, brought him to the goal of life.

356Then Prabhu showed mercy to Vrindavana Dasa:
his fame as a kaviraja spread through the world.

357Then Prabhu showed mercy to Nimai Kaviraja,
the brother of Rupa Kaviraja, renowned in the world.

358He chants a hundred thousand names of Hari, counting them,
and dances in sankirtana, immersed in happiness.

359In ecstasy his body grows limp, he cries out again and again,
leaps and bounds, and every moment roars.

360Streams of tears flow from his eyes unceasingly,
his body is covered with gooseflesh, sweat always flows.

361Then he showed mercy to Srimanta Chakravarti:
receiving the shelter of his feet, he became renowned.

362He takes a hundred thousand names of Hari and has faith in the name;
he is a fine connoisseur of rasa and indifferent to the world.

363Then Prabhu showed mercy to Sri Raghunandana:
showing him mercy, Prabhu was filled with joy.

364Then he showed mercy to Gauranga Dasa:
who can describe his countless virtues?

365He always takes Hari-nama with a mind absorbed in bhava
and always remembers the lotus feet of his Prabhu.

366He always takes Hari-nama
and always remembers the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.

367Saying "Rupa, Sanatana", he cries out again and again;
as soon as he says "Bhatta Gosani", tears flow.

368As soon as he says "Gauranga", his mind is absorbed in bhava,
and at once he meditates on the lotus feet of his Prabhu.

369Srimanta Thakura, born in a brahmana family —
to him Prabhu showed mercy, joyful at heart.

370Prabhu showed mercy to Gopijanavallabha:
he is a maha-bhagavata whose (fame) spread through the world.

371His bhajana cannot be told:
he is deeply absorbed in service in the mind.

372Then Prabhu showed mercy to Sri Chaitanya Dasa:
as soon as he says "Sri Krishna Chaitanya", he floats in prema.

373Then Prabhu showed mercy to one named Sri Govinda:
as soon as he says "Sri Gauranga", he becomes mad with prema.

374To Tulasirama Dasa, born in a weaver family,
(he showed mercy); he always remembers Prabhu's feet with great longing.

375Balarama Dasa was born in the land of Utkala;
he is born in a brahmana family and indifferent to the world.

376Then Prabhu showed mercy to Chaudhuri Dayarama;
both were born in brahmana families and live in the same village.

377How great their mutual love was cannot be told;
he surrendered everything at his Prabhu's own feet.

378One of his royal devotees is Sri Harivallabha,
known as "Sarkar" — rare in the world.

379Prabhu, filled with mercy, showed him mercy;
his way of bhajana cannot be described.

380Another disciple of Prabhu is Krishnavallabha Chakravarti:
receiving Prabhu's mercy, he became most wise.

381To Sri Krishna Purohita, a resident of Gauda,
he showed mercy, filled with compassion.

382To Shyama Bhatta of the same land he showed mercy;
the disciples and grand-disciples of the two filled the world.

383There too lived Sri Jayarama Chakravarti,
who became renowned as "Premi Jayarama" ("loving Jayarama").

384Then Prabhu showed mercy to Thakuradasa Thakura,
whose way of bhajana is most profound.

385A resident of Mathura is Sri Mathuradasa,
born in a brahmana family, full of great joy.

386Sri Shyamasundara Dasa is a simple-hearted brahmana
who takes a hundred thousand names of Hari.

387Prabhu showed mercy to Sri Atmarama;
the three, living in one place, came to love each other dearly.

388A resident of Vrindavana, a store of great happiness,
named Vrindavana Dasa, a treasury of great virtues:

389to him Prabhu, the treasury of virtues, showed mercy.
What can I, dull-witted, say of his virtues?

390Then he showed mercy to Govindarama:
with great concern Prabhu made him his own.

391Then he showed mercy to Sri Gopala Dasa;
the three live in one place and float in great bliss.

392Three great and composed devotees live at Sri Kunda:35
Prabhu, steady in mercy, showed mercy to the three.

393Sri Mohana Dasa and Vrajananda Dasa,
Sri Hari Prasada and Sukhananda Dasa,

394loving Harirama and Muktarama Dasa —
ever faithful to Prabhu's feet, with joy in their hearts.

395All of them perform bhajana together,
all take a hundred thousand names of Hari.

396I cannot describe the summit of their bhajana:
they always remain absorbed in service in the mind.

397In Bengal (Vanga) lives one named Kalanidhi,
born in a brahmana family, with the title "Acharya":

398to him Prabhu mercifully showed mercy.
Another of his disciples is named Ramasharana.

399Premadasa and Rasikadasa are brothers,
both most eager in the service of the Vaishnavas.

400In the land of Vishnupura very many live:
the disciples became so many that they cannot be written down.

401Living in his own land, he made very many disciples;
their names I, the foremost of fools, do not know.

402From various lands near and far many
came, and all became vessels of mercy.

403Rarh, Vanga and Gauda — all those lands,
the land of Vraja, Magadha and the land of Utkala,

404the far side of the Great Ganga, Vriddha-kankal,36
and all the lands along the Ganga —

405his disciples, their disciples and theirs in turn —
all took shelter: so it has been told in brief.

406Who can tell all his disciples?
I have said only a little, to point the way.

407Who can count all the disciples and grand-disciples?
Only the Thousand-mouthed (Shesha) might somehow do so.

408Briefly I have told of Prabhu's branches,
by remembering whom one obtains Krishna-prema.

409Krishna and Krishna's devotees are alike in their deeds;
for my own purification I sing their song.

410Whoever reads and hears this is fortunate:
without effort Krishna-prema appears in him.

411This narrative of the Karnananda is an extract (niryasa) of nectar:
at its touch on the ear, the joy of prema is born in the devotees.

412The daughter of Sri Acharya Prabhu is Srila Hemalata:
has not the Creator fashioned a wish-fulfilling creeper of prema?

413Her two lotus feet sport in my heart;
Yadunandana Dasa tells the rasa of the Karnananda.

Thus ends the first niryasa of the Sri Karnananda, called "The Description of the Branches of Sri Acharya Prabhu".

Notes

  1. A verse of Srila Rupa Gosvami (Vidagdha-madhava 1.2), also quoted in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Adi 1.4).
  2. "Leads to the goal of parakiya" attempts the rare parakīyārtha-sārthinam. According to Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, parakiya-bhava is the eternal transcendental mood of the gopis in Vraja, whose taste the followers of Rupa attain in the service of the manjaris; it has nothing to do with mundane "illicit love".
  3. "Hundreds of thousands" (laksha grantha): here grantha is the counting unit of text (32 syllables, i.e. a "verse"), as in the traditional reckoning of the Gosvamis' works; cf. CC Madhya 1.
  4. Krishnadasa Kaviraja, author of the Chaitanya-charitamrita.
  5. The Prema-vilasa (vilasas 18 and 20) and the Bhakti-ratnakara (13) give the same two marriages of Srinivasa (to Draupadi-Ishvari and Padmavati-Gauranga-priya); the names are not given here.
  6. A list of the Gosvamis' books: the Toshani is the Vaishnava-toshani (Sanatana's commentary on the Tenth Canto); the Dashama-charita, Gitavali, Virudavali (part of the Stavavali) and Mukta-charita are works of Rupa, Sanatana and Raghunatha Dasa; the Brahma-samhita and Krishna-karnamrita are books Mahaprabhu found in the South; the Gopi-premamrita is probably the text commented on by Krishnadasa Kaviraja; the Madhava-mahotsava is a poem by Jiva Gosvami.
  7. Yama is the same as prahara, about three hours (as the editor also explains).
  8. The Jagannatha-vallabha-nataka of Ramananda Raya.
  9. Thakura Mahashaya is Narottama Dasa Thakura. Karnapura Kaviraja is a disciple of Srinivasa, author of a Sanskrit list of his branches; not to be confused with Kavi Karnapura (Paramananda Sena), son of Shivananda Sena.
  10. "My Prabhu" is the author's spiritual master; further on the author calls himself the servant of Hemalata Thakurani, Srinivasa's daughter (cf. the colophons). Payar is the Bengali couplet metre.
  11. Digvijayi, a title of a scholar victorious in debate. Ramachandra Kaviraja was the son of Chiranjiva Sena; in the Prema-vilasa and the Bhakti-ratnakara too he meets Srinivasa in Yajigrama while returning from his wedding — an episode common to all three sources. Here his home is given as Kumaranagara.
  12. Literally "do not work maya on my scorched life", i.e. do not feign indifference, do not push me away.
  13. The subject is not named; from the sense, Srinivasa orders Govinda Kaviraja (the poet Govindadasa) to compose padas.
  14. Divyasimha is the son of Govinda Kaviraja (as the editor also notes).
  15. On parakiya-bhava see note 2.
  16. Kanchanagaria (Kanchana-Nagariya) is a village near Yajigrama; in the Bhakti-ratnakara Sri Dasa and Gokula Dasa of Kanchanagaria are disciples of Srinivasa.
  17. Sri Ishvarer, perhaps a slip for Sri Ishvarir (Ishvari Thakurani, Srinivasa's wife; cf. 179), or "Ishvara" is Prabhu himself.
  18. According to the Karnananda, Hemalata is the wife of Gopijanavallabha Chattaraja, and Krishnapriya the wife of Chaitanya Chattaraja (158).
  19. Varna-vipra (varna-brahmana): a brahmana who serves as priest to lower castes; hence Gopala Dasa is told to "deliver his own community" (literally "his own jati").
  20. That is, to keep from falling asleep: if the head nods, the cord pulls the hair.
  21. Cf. 66: Karnapura Kaviraja is the author of the Sanskrit list of Srinivasa's branches on which Yadunandana relies.
  22. Ghataka: a marriage-broker; evidently the hereditary occupation of the family.
  23. In the Prema-vilasa Srinivasa's fathers-in-law are Gopala Dasa (Gopala Chakravarti), father of Draupadi-Ishvari, and Raghu Chakravarti, father of Padmavati-Gauranga-priya.
  24. Vanamali Dasa is the son of Sri Gopala Dasa (see 230). The order of names in the list, as the author himself warns (74), is not always consistent.
  25. Purushottama is Jagannatha in Puri. According to the Prema-vilasa (12–13) and the Bhakti-ratnakara (7), the Gosvamis' books were stolen by Vira Hambira's men while Srinivasa, Narottama and Shyamananda were carrying them from Vrindavana to Gauda; here the theft takes place during Srinivasa's pilgrimage to Puri, and Narottama and Shyamananda are not mentioned.
  26. According to the editor's gloss, Srimati is Hemalata Thakurani, Srinivasa's daughter and the author's guru.
  27. Karana: Kayasthas (scribes); the editor's long footnote on the origin of the castes is not translated.
  28. Bishvas (vishvasa, "trust"): the family title of a trusted scribe or steward.
  29. In the Bhakti-ratnakara (7) too, Srinivasa is brought to Vira Hambira's court by a brahmana of the village of Deuli with whom he was staying; there he is called Krishnavallabha, here Sri Vallabha Thakura.
  30. Kalachand ("the Dark Moon"): the Deity of Krishna served by Vira Hambira in Vishnupura (Sri Kalachand).
  31. A song of Vira Hambira (signed "this Vira Hambira" in the last stanza). "You made me a maidservant" (dasi): service in the spiritual form of a maidservant (manjari) of Sri Radha is the goal of raganuga-bhajana according to Rupa Gosvami and Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati; "Gora" is Gauranga. Cf. the songs of Vira Hambira in the Bhakti-ratnakara (7).
  32. A song in the voice of a gopi (Sri Radha) suffering separation from Krishna: the "mother-in-law and sister-in-law" and "master of the house" are images of the parakiya-rasa of Vraja. According to Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati this is transcendental prema, having nothing in common with mundane passion.
  33. The classic instruction of raganuga-bhakti (Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 1.2.295): in the siddha-deha — the spiritual form inwardly conceived according to the guru's instruction — service is performed in the mind, and with the external body one performs hearing, chanting and the other practices of sadhana-bhakti. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati stressed that the siddha-deha is revealed by the guru's mercy as the heart is purified, not wilfully imagined; the "kama-gayatri" and "kama-bija" are mantras of service to Krishna, unrelated to mundane kama.
  34. According to the Prema-vilasa (13), Vira Hambira receives the name Haricharana Dasa; here it is "Gopaladasa", given by Sri Jiva.
  35. Sri Kunda is Radha-kunda. "Three" are mentioned, but more names are listed (393–394).
  36. "The far side of the Great Ganga" probably means the lands beyond the Padma (East Bengal). Vriddha-kankal: the name is unclear (a district?); transliterated.
